Convert files on the phone to take less space: hi-res FLAC to CD-quality FLAC, or to AAC

FLAC is already compressed without loss — squeezing it harder saves 1–3 %, not more. Real savings come from two places: hi-res files (24-bit) take almost twice as much as CD quality and sound the same; and AAC at 256 kbps is indistinguishable from the original for nearly everyone in blind tests, at a quarter of the size. Conversion runs on the phone, offline.
Only hi-res files change. Still FLAC, still lossless relative to a CD; the extra detail of 24-bit is beyond what people hear.
About 4× smaller than FLAC. Transparent for nearly everyone on any headphones. Lossy: going back means FLAC versions (for tracks on Yandex).
About 8× smaller. Fine for speakers and the commute; an attentive ear on good headphones may notice.
